reason: The bone framework has spaces awaiting mineral, and the mineral picture shows resistance to compression.
expectation: The mineral should strengthen the living bones.

alternatives.reason: The cells also fit the pictured space between the front tendons.

effect: The mineral strengthened the bones while leaving the joint able to move; the remaining goal is to build the muscles.
reaction: The contrast between hard bone and the movable joint makes sense.
reason: The front tendon attachments show a space for muscle cells between them.
expectation: The cells should form a muscle between the front attachments.

alternatives.reason: The back attachments also have a space for muscle cells.

effect: The front cells formed the biceps, which pulls to bend the elbow. The back attachment still needs muscle.
reaction: The picture makes the connection between the muscle's position and bending clear.
reason: The back attachments have the remaining space for muscle cells on the opposite side of the elbow.
expectation: The cells should form a back muscle that pulls the elbow in the opposite direction.

effect: The back muscle became the triceps, confirming that its attachments let the same kind of cells pull the elbow straight. Both goals are complete.
reaction: It was satisfying to see how position changes the direction of the pull.

mostWorthwhile.text: Building the biceps and triceps was most worthwhile because their opposite attachments explain bending and straightening without needing different kinds of pulling cells.

leastWorthwhile.text: Adding mineral was straightforward and less engaging than comparing the muscles, though it clearly showed why bone is hard while the joint stays movable.

surprise.text: The same kind of muscle cells can produce opposite movements because of where the muscles attach.

arbitrary.text: No action felt arbitrary: the pictured spaces and goals made the pairings clear.

continue.text: I would choose to try another chapter because seeing the parts assembled helped explain how their positions affect movement, although these choices were fairly obvious.
